 Boldr is the first global B-Corp dedicated to delivering world-class Client experiences while creating
 access to dignified, meaningful work in communities around the world.

 impact.
 LET’S START WITH OUR VALUES
 Excellent . Being excellent at what we do sets us apart. It happens when we care about our work and how it lands, set clear standards, and hold each other accountable. We don't stop at meeting the standard; we keep raising the bar.
 Authentic . Real connection happens when we show up as our best, truest selves, help others dothe same, and stand by each other through the harder times.
 Curious . Curiosity keeps us innovative. Better understanding comes from asking helpful questions, seeking to understand before we act, and building on each other's thinking.
 Dynamic . Growth is central to our purpose, and it only happens in dynamic environments where we stay flexible, adaptable and open.
 Empathetic . Great partnerships happen when we take the time to understand the people we work with, our teams, our clients and our communities, for better outcomes for each.
 WHAT IS YOUR ROLE
 As Senior Director, People Operations, you are the operational and governance backbone of Boldr's People function. You own the systems, rewards, and standards that let a five-country division run with consistency and care.
 Three connected disciplines roll up to you across the Philippines, South Africa, Mexico, Canada, and the United States:
 People Operations and Systems : the employee lifecycle, our HRIS (Rippling), people data, service delivery, and self-service.
 Total Rewards : compensation and benefits, Living Wage governance, pay equity, and job banding.
 Business Partnering : ER cases and investigations, multi-country labor law compliance, risk and audit, and the policies and handbooks that keep us fair and consistent.

The longer-range strategic agenda, organizational design, performance strategy, and strategic business partnering, sits with the VP and grows alongside our People Success team. Your mandate is to make the backbone genuinely excellent: scalable processes that do not rely on heroics, clean and trustworthy data, sound compliance across every jurisdiction, and a team member experience that reflects our values wherever people work.
 You report to the VP, People, and you are one of the leaders the rest of the division depends on to keep the engine running as we scale.
 WHY DO WE WANT YOU
 We are looking for an impact-driven operator who can give a fast-growing, five-country division the backbone it needs to scale without breaking. Someone who builds systems that last, holds a high bar on compliance and fairness, and still keeps the human center in every process they design.
 You will protect organizational health, bring calm and consistency to sensitive moments, and make the everyday experience of working at Boldr feel reliable and fair in every country we operate in. We do all of this so our team members can thrive as we grow.
 WHAT WILL YOU DO
 People Operations and Systems
 Own the employee lifecycle end-to-end: onboarding, changes, and offboarding, delivered consistently across all five countries.
 Lead Rippling as our HRIS and system of record; design and maintain clean workflows, self-service, and service delivery (ticketing and knowledge base).
 Establish data integrity and reporting discipline: headcount, attrition, and the people data leaders rely on to decide well.
 Partner closely with Payroll to protect accuracy and timeliness in every jurisdiction.
 Modernize People infrastructure through automation and sound system design, so support scales without manual workarounds.

 Direct compensation cycles with rigor and clarity: timelines, manager enablement, auditability, and clear communication.
 Oversee job banding and pay structures using our market data source (Payfactors), keeping pay equitable and defensible.
 Steward pay equity and transparency norms that build trust while managing risk appropriately.
 Employee Relations

 Build the ER frameworks and manager guidance that keep outcomes fair and well-documented across countries.
 Serve as a trusted, high-integrity escalation point on difficult people matters.
 Compliance, Risk, and Governance
 Ensure compliance across all five countries and both operating models: Managed Outsourcing and Global Employment (EoR).
 Own records, audit, and data protection for People data.
 Translate local labor realities into sound, consistent decisions, flag clearly where in-country counsel is needed, and engage and consult with counsel on these matters .
 Build the governance and risk frameworks that let us scale responsibly.
 Policy Development and Maintenance
 Own the development, maintenance, and governance of People policies and employee handbooks.
 Keep policy current with changing labor law in each jurisdiction, and consistent with our values and B Corp commitments.
 Make policy clear, accessible, and genuinely useful to managers and team members, not just technically compliant.
 Team Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership
 Lead and develop the People Operations, Total Rewards, and Business Partnering teams; set clear goals, coach for growth, and build a culture of service excellence.

 Partner with the VP, the Talent Acquisition and People Success pillars, Business Operations, Finance, and client-facing teams to keep the backbone aligned to the business and company strategy .

 Work with a globally distributed team of experienced engineers focused on the vector search capabilities of Elasticsearch.

 Write idiomatic modern Java -- Elasticsearch is 99.8% Java!

Sadie is building technology for hospitality.
 We're looking for an account executive to win new restaurant customers in Vancouver or Calgary, and to run every deal yourself from the first lead to the signed agreement.
 This is a field role. You'll find restaurants through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits, then meet owners in person and show them Sadie working on their own calls. You'll work with onboarding and customer success, so that what you sell goes live well. You'll carry monthly and quarterly targets and own the forecast behind them.
 You decide where to spend your time and which deals to pursue, within agreed pricing and terms. AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research restaurants before a visit, prepare demos, draft proposals and follow-ups, and plan your territory. You're responsible for the quality of everything that goes out under your name.
 What we value
 Sound judgement about which deals are real.
 Taking responsibility for your number and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how a restaurant makes money, and caring whether Sadie improves it.
 Curiosity about why a deal was lost, and a willingness to change your approach.
 The honesty to say a deal is slipping before the forecast says it for you.
 What you'll do
 Win new restaurants, from first visit to signed agreement 
 Most of your time goes on live deals, and most of those deals happen in person. You'll sit down with owners and general managers in their restaurants to learn how the phone is handled today: who answers it, what gets missed during service, and what those missed calls cost in bookings and orders. Then you'll demo Sadie against that picture.
 You'll scope what the restaurant needs, write the proposal, negotiate terms and get the agreement signed. 
 Most of the judgement is in qualification. A good demo with someone who can't sign, or a restaurant Sadie can't serve yet, costs you weeks. You're expected to spot that early and move on.
 Build your own pipeline across your territory 
 You'll generate your own leads through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits. That means planning which neighbourhoods and restaurant groups to work, walking in at the right time of day, and following up until you get a meeting.
 Hit your targets with a forecast you can defend 
 You're measured against monthly and quarterly sales targets, and the expectation is that you hit them consistently. You'll keep every opportunity accurate in HubSpot, so that stage, value and close date mean something to the people who plan around them.
 Represent Sadie where restaurant people meet 
 You'll attend local industry events, restaurant meetups and trade shows across your geography. You'll decide which ones are worth the evening, run the conversations there, and turn them into meetings within the week.
 For a lot of operators, you'll be the first person from Sadie they meet. What they hear from you is what they'll repeat to other owners.
 Hand over accounts that go live well 
 The restaurant buys Sadie, but the guest ringing to book a table decides whether it works. You'll give onboarding and customer success a written record of what you promised, what the owner expects, and what could go wrong.
 If you oversell, the owner finds out on a Friday night and the guest pays for it. Set expectations you can stand behind.
 What you'll bring
 At least 2 years in a closing sales role, selling software or services to businesses in hospitality (ideally full service restaurants) or experience working at full service restaurants.
 A record of meeting targets, and the ability to explain how you did it.
 Experience running the whole cycle yourself, from prospecting through to signature.
 Comfort with in-person selling, including cold visits and demos in front of a busy owner.
 Strong discovery skills. You can find out what an operator needs in fifteen minutes between services.
 Clear written communication. Your proposals and follow-ups are accurate and short.
 An honest forecast. You'd rather call a deal lost than carry it for another month.
 You use AI every day for research, preparation and drafting, and you check what it produces.
 You organise your own week across a territory and follow through without being managed.
 Useful experience
 Selling to restaurants or other hospitality operators.
 Working in a restaurant yourself, front of house or in management.
 Selling reservations, POS, telephony or other restaurant technology.
 An existing network among restaurant owners in your territory.
 Selling AI products to non-technical buyers.
 Being an early sales hire at a startup.
 Who will enjoy this role
 You like finding out how a business really works. When an owner says they miss calls at seven on a Saturday, you want to know how many, what those calls were for, and what happened to the guest who hung up.
 In a single week you might walk into six restaurants before lunch service, run a demo at a bar between shifts, spend an evening at a trade show, and sit with onboarding to sort out an account you signed. Your schedule follows the restaurant day, and some of your best conversations will happen at three in the afternoon or late at night.
 The hard parts are specific. Owners are busy and sceptical, and many will turn you away mid-service. You'll hear no far more often than yes, and you'll still need to be back through the next door the same afternoon. Some of the material you'd expect to have, such as local case studies or a settled playbook, may not exist yet, and you'll help build it while carrying a number.
 Why this role matters
 Sadie is building technology for hospitality. Restaurants lose revenue to calls nobody picks up, and our product exists to answer them.
 This role is how Sadie reaches the restaurants in your geography. You decide who to visit and how each customer starts. The agreements you sign affect revenue, what onboarding and customer success inherit, and what a guest hears when they ring to book a table.
 You'll own new restaurant business across your territory, with the authority to decide how Sadie wins it.
 #Sadie

About AmpThink 
 AmpThink is a Master Technology Integrator — we design and deploy the technology behind many of North America’s premier sports and entertainment venues, spanning wired and wireless networking, LED and large-format displays, IPTV, and audio/visual systems. Our customers include major sports organizations such as Maple Leafs Sports & Entertainment, the Calgary Flames, and the Buffalo Bills. Our Canadian operations run from our office in Fort Erie, Ontario, working hand-in-hand with our head office in Garland, Texas.
 The Role 
 We are hiring an Accountant (CPA) to manage the books and the day-to-day operations of our Canadian office in Fort Erie — a senior, accounting-led role with a light set of office-management duties on top. You will own the Canadian entity’s books, handle Canadian tax and payroll remittances, and be our on-the-ground financial contact for “all things Canada,” reporting to AmpThink’s CFO in Garland, Texas. Because AmpThink’s work is building the technology inside major sports and entertainment venues, the numbers you keep sit behind real projects at real venues.
 This is a genuinely cross-border opportunity. You will maintain a Canadian set of books that reports up to a U.S. parent — reconciling intercompany activity, working in both CAD and USD, and bridging Canadian requirements (GST/HST and CRA payroll remittances) with U.S. head-office processes. If you enjoy operating at the intersection of two countries’ accounting and tax systems, this role offers that variety every day.
 AmpThink’s Canadian Practice lead is based here in Fort Erie but travels frequently, so day to day you will often be the on-site presence keeping the office and the books running — with the Practice lead and our U.S. finance team a call away. This is an on-site role well suited to someone in the Niagara region who wants a stable seat close to home, without the daily commute to Toronto.
 The ideal candidate is a designated CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant) with strong, current accounting skills who is happy to wear a few hats in a small-office setting. If you have construction or project-based accounting experience, even better — it maps directly to how AmpThink runs its venue projects.
 This is a newly created position. 
 What You Will Do 
 Own the full cycle of accounting for the Canadian entity — accounts payable and receivable, bank and general-ledger reconciliations, and journal entries — and support month-end and year-end close with clean, organized records
 Assist with US bookkeeping and accounting in partnership with the CFO as time allows
 Prepare and remit Canadian GST/HST and payroll source deductions to the CRA, or coordinate them with head office and external advisors
 Work across the border with head office in Garland, Texas — reconcile intercompany activity, handle CAD/USD transactions, and keep U.S. leadership current on Canadian financial matters
 Track recurring charges, review and code incoming bills, and route them to the right approvers
 Help schedule field resources and track their time, attendance, and expenses in AmpThink’s Zoho tools
 Keep the small Fort Erie office running — mail, supplies, vendors, filing, and records
 Occasionally receive materials at the loading dock — sign for deliveries, move items with a manual pallet jack, and lift up to 50 lbs (23 kg)
 How We Use AI in This Process 
 AmpThink uses artificial intelligence to help screen and assess applications against the criteria for this role. AI does not make the final decision: our CFO reviews every application, with the benefit of that AI analysis, before any candidate is ruled out.
 What You Bring 
 CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant) designation, with strong, hands-on full-cycle accounting experience — AP/AR, reconciliations, journal entries, and month-end/year-end close
 Working knowledge of Canadian GST/HST and payroll source-deduction / CRA remittances
 Proficiency with a cloud accounting/ERP system and strong Excel skills — we run on Zoho (Books, People, Projects, Expense); QuickBooks, Sage, or Xero experience transfers well
 Comfort coordinating with a head office in another country and working across CAD and USD
 Genuine comfort working independently — self-directed, organized, and reliable, since the Canadian Practice lead travels frequently
 A willingness to carry light office-management duties — mail, receiving, and coordination — alongside the books
 Able to lift up to 50 lbs (23 kg) and operate a manual pallet jack for occasional receiving
 Clear written and verbal communication
 Legally entitled to work in Canada; able to pass a background and reference check
 Nice to Have 
 Construction, technology-integration, or other project-based accounting experience — job costing, work-in-progress (WIP), and progress billing
 Cross-border or intercompany accounting experience, or exposure to both Canadian and U.S. tax and reporting
 Experience with multi-currency (CAD/USD) transactions and reconciliations
 Experience in a sports, venue, or large-project environment
 Experience owning the books for a small entity or branch, or running a small or solo office
 Familiarity with the Zoho suite
 Extended health benefits (after a 90-day waiting period). Contributions to Canadian savings plan. Three weeks of paid vacation per year. Paid statutory holidays. Paid volunteer days through the AmpForce program. Company gear program.

Boulangeries ANGE est une chaîne de boulangeries-pâtisseries artisanales qui allie tradition et modernité pour offrir à nos clients une expérience gourmande inégalée. Notre engagement envers la qualité et l'authenticité a fait de nous l'un des leaders du secteur de la boulangerie en France.
Raison d’être du poste
Assurer la gestion des ressources humaines pour soutenir la croissance de l’entreprise, en veillant à un recrutement efficace, au développement des compétences et à la conformité des pratiques RH. 

Vos principales missions: Concevoir, implanter et faire évoluer les processus RH clés pour soutenir notre croissance.
 Garantir la conformité légale en matière de droit du travail et d’obligations RH.
 Piloter le recrutement de A à Z, incluant le recrutement international de boulangers.
 Accompagner les gestionnaires dans la gestion disciplinaire et le développement de leurs équipes.
 Suivre et gérer les permis de travail, invalidités et accidents de travail.
 Développer et maintenir les outils, politiques et documents RH.
 Assurer la coordination avec la paie et gérer les avantages sociaux.
 Mettre en place des programmes de développement des compétences et de formations obligatoires.
 Proposer et déployer des initiatives de coaching en gestion.
 Optimiser et formaliser les pratiques RH pour plus d’efficacité.
Profil recherché: Expérience confirmée (3 à 5 ans) en ressources humaines.
 Solides compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles.
 Sens de l’autonomie, capacité à jongler avec plusieurs priorités.
 Connaissance approfondie du droit du travail canadien.
 Passion pour le développement des talents et l’accompagnement des équipes.
 Maîtrise de l’anglais non requise.
Ce que nous offrons: Avantages complets : assurances dentaires, invalidité, maladie complémentaire et vie.
 Congés payés et horaires flexibles.
 Indemnité de déplacement et stationnement gratuit.
 Repas à prix réduit ou gratuit.
 Tenue décontractée et ambiance conviviale.
